card: This pull request raises the project's minimum C++ language standard from C++20 to C++23, increasing compiler toolchain requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It retires internal polyfills like util::Expected and custom byteswap helpers in favor of std::expected and std::byteswap, drops legacy template workarounds, and updates string searches to std::string::contains across 56 files. The author argues that workarounds to avoid C++23 continue to accumulate while downstream libraries like libmultiprocess already use C++23 features. This is submitted as an RFC draft to explore compiler readiness and unblocks work tracked in #34979.
changed_since_previous: Added commit to fix IWYU (include-what-you-use) header inclusion heuristics after removing util/expected.h.
evidence: PR description: 'workarounds to avoid C++23 keep accumulating and some parts of the code already use C++23 features, such as lambda attributes (https://github.com/bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess/commit/bdd0cd69418d189f62699d274a751cbf6d36bb43).'
PR description notes it unlocks future work discussed in issue #34979.
problem: Maintaining compatibility with C++20 forces developers to keep custom polyfills, template workarounds, and verbose idiom patterns in the codebase even as adjacent dependencies like libmultiprocess already rely on C++23 features.

risk.why: Raising compiler requirements and replacing low-level endian/byteswap routines could introduce build breakage on supported distributions or subtle compiler-specific code generation defects.

scope_notes: Contains large mechanical replacements across 56 files, including migrating string search expressions to std::string::contains and updating includes for std::expected.
summary: This pull request bumps the required C++ standard to C++23 across CMake, depends, and CI, raising minimum compiler requirements to GCC 13 and Clang 19. It replaces internal polyfills with standard library features, specifically migrating util::Expected to std::expected, using std::byteswap, and dropping the ALWAYS_FALSE workaround. In addition, it modernizes code paths across the project using C++23 features like std::views::zip and std::string::contains.
